summary:
Cosmic Health Baba is an onboard medical decision-support and crew readiness application developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Designed for deep-space missions where real-time communication with Earth flight surgeons is delayed by up to 40 minutes, the software enables non-physician astronauts to monitor their health independently and respond effectively during emergencies.
The platform integrates four core operational modules: a Daily Biometric Check-in that validates heart rate, blood oxygen (SpO_2), sleep, and temperature against each astronaut's personal pre-flight baseline; a Longitudinal Health Trends tracker that flags multi-day physiological drift before acute symptoms emerge; an automated Crew Board that redistributes strenuous mission tasks from fatigued crewmates to nominal peers; and an interactive Emergency Protocol assistant featuring voice-guided microgravity triage trees (including Evetts-Russomano CPR) alongside a light-delay downlink packet generator.
By translating complex physiological telemetry into clear, actionable guidance, Cosmic Health Baba directly mitigates the five hazards of human spaceflight empowering crews to preserve mission readiness, prevent cascading fatigue, and manage critical medical events autonomously in deep space and remote environments on Earth.
details:
Cosmic Health Baba is an autonomous onboard medical decision-support and crew readiness system developed for deep-space missions where real-time communication with Earth-based flight surgeons is unavailable or delayed by up to 40 minutes. Designed specifically for non-physician astronauts, the platform transforms complex physiological telemetry into clear, actionable operational guidance across four integrated modules.

How It Works

  • Daily Biometric Check-in & Validation: Crew members log four core vital signs—heart rate (bpm), blood oxygen saturation (SpO2\text{SpO}_2SpO2​), sleep duration (hours), and core body temperature (°C). Strict range-checking logic prevents erroneous entries, while an evaluation engine compares each metric against that specific astronaut's pre-flight baseline rather than generic population averages.
  • Longitudinal Health Trends: Using cached time-series visualizations, the system tracks multi-day mission telemetry against personalized baselines and clinical threshold zones. A moving-average drift detector alerts the crew whenever a parameter deviates by 15% or more over three consecutive days, catching gradual physiological deconditioning or sleep deficits before they escalate.
  • Crew Board & Task Redistribution: The operational board synthesizes individual vital assessments into clear crew readiness statuses (Ready, Needs Rest, or At Risk). When a crewmate is compromised, a baseline-proximity matching algorithm automatically suggests reassigning their strenuous mission tasks (such as EVA preparation or reactor maintenance) to the healthiest available peer—capping reassignments at one task per helper to prevent cascading fatigue.
  • Autonomous Emergency Protocol: During acute medical events (such as chest pain or unresponsiveness), the emergency copilot provides step-by-step interactive triage trees paired with browser-based text-to-speech audio guidance so responders can keep their hands free. It incorporates microgravity-specific resuscitation protocols—such as the Evetts-Russomano anchor method and Crew Medical Restraint System transitions—alongside a configurable Lunar/Mars light-delay countdown clock and an automated telemetry downlink report generator.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Mission Autonomy & Crew Safety: Empowers crews on Artemis lunar missions and Mars transits to detect subtle health changes early, balance daily operational workloads safely, and execute life-saving emergency interventions without waiting for ground control.
  • Earth-Based Applications: Beyond spaceflight, the lightweight, offline-capable architecture offers a practical blueprint for remote medical triage and preventive health monitoring in isolated communities, polar research stations, maritime vessels, and low-resource clinics on Earth.

Tools, Technologies & Creativity

  • Software & Stack: Built in Python using Gradio for reactive state management and user interface orchestration, Matplotlib (with server-side LRU caching) for dynamic telemetry visualization, Pillow for asset optimization, and custom CSS styled around high-contrast Mission Control aesthetics. Hosted live on Hugging Face Spaces with open-source version control on GitHub.
  • Creative Approach: Rather than treating astronauts as medical experts or overwhelming them with raw clinical charts, we combined individualized baseline drift analytics, automated workload-balancing algorithms, hands-free voice triage, and an approachable mission identity (Cosmic Health Baba) to reduce cognitive load during high-stress emergencies.

Key Design Factors Considered

  • Individualized Baselines Over Static Norms: Spaceflight alters human physiology differently for each astronaut; comparing readings against personal pre-flight baselines yields far more accurate early warnings.
  • Human Factors & Cognitive Load: High-contrast dark-mode cards, color-coded status indicators, strict input validation, and spoken emergency instructions ensure rapid comprehension under fatigue or crisis conditions.
  • Communication Latency & Reliability: All diagnostic logic runs locally without relying on external cloud APIs during triage, while explicit light-delay timers reinforce the operational reality that immediate action must be taken onboard before Earth can reply.
